text: What if every atom of iron vanished right now Not rust Not
just steel All of it The trains stop Towers twist And the
iron in your blood stops carrying oxygen Day one The lights flicker
then fail Bridges lose their bones Cars become useless shells Inside your
body hemoglobin drops its iron so oxygen has nowhere to ride People
collapse in seconds The modern world does not burn It falls apart
Day seven Farms freeze in place Tractors are dead metal plows are
gone and fences are missing There are no steel tools to plant
harvest or can food Supermarkets empty in days By day thirty hospitals
are overwhelmed No iron means no hemoglobin no surgical steel no machines
to keep the wounded alive Day ninety Civilization steps backward Cities become
quiet ruins People trade metal for memory Wooden wheels stone knives bone
needles clay pots We learn to make fire without lighters and build
shelter without nails Every old photo shows a world that suddenly looks
impossible Day three hundred sixty five A new world Villages rise beside
the ruins Children learn which stones spark which roots heal and how
to shape a branch into a bow There is no iron in
their future Survival is slower louder and closer to the ground But
here is the twist Iron is not a metal we invented It
is forged in dying stars carried in our blood and buried in
the earth Remove it and a single year is enough to turn
us into strangers on our own planet
